subject: Retention carve-outs for marketplace backup windows
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@greenbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: GreenBank IT <itops@greenbank.com>
Date: 2025-04-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Retention carve-outs for marketplace backup windows

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this — we're moving GreenBank's marketplace integration toward a pilot and security wants clarity on a few retention items before procurement signs off. High-level asks: 
- Confirm Redwood's timelines for primary data deletion (customer-initiated deletes) vs. snapshot/backups that may contain customer PII.
- Do backups/snapshots follow the same 90-day retention as active data, or do you have a longer backup purge window (we've seen vendors keep snapshots longer for RTO reasons)?
- We also need to understand the deletion workflow: how are deletion requests propagated to backups and metadata indexes? Is there an audit trail we can review?
- For incident debugging we sometimes require short-term retention of detailed logs/traces. Would Redwood support a per-customer debug-trace carve-out (e.g., 30–60 days) that is auditable and isolated?
- Finally, please provide an updated subprocessor list and whether data could be transferred outside US/EU under these flows.

We need these answers to scope a small DPA amendment. Can you attach whatever you have (retention table, subprocessors, DPA language)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — legal/procurement are on a tight timeline.

Best,
Anita
Security PM, GreenBank
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@greenbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carve-outs for marketplace backup windows

Hi Anita — thanks, this is a helpful summary. Quick summary of Redwood's current position and what I'll attach: proposed_retention_table.xlsx (technical timelines) and a DPA amendment draft to capture the carve-outs.

Summary (short):
- Active customer data: default retention for application data is 90 days unless customer configures otherwise. Customer-initiated deletion requests remove active copies and metadata within 90 days.
- Backups/snapshots: we keep immutable snapshots for disaster recovery; standard lifecycle currently purges snapshots within 120 days from creation. Snapshots can contain PII until purged.
- Deletion workflow: deletion request triggers metadata purge + tombstone in active store; background job reconciles snapshots against a deletion index and schedules snapshot object expiry via lifecycle rules. We can provide proof points/audit events for deletion which include timestamps and object ids.
- Debug logs: we can support a per-customer debug-trace bucket with a configurable TTL; recommended default for exceptions is 45 days (fits between your 30–60d ask); access can be scoped to a small set of roles and require approval.
- Subprocessors: I'll attach the current subprocessors PDF; most common are AWS (S3/EBS), GCP (for non-hosted regions), CloudFlare/Edge CDN, Datadog (optional telemetry).

Next steps: Marcus and Monica, can you confirm the technical feasibility of guaranteeing deletion timestamps for snapshots and whether 120 days is a hard limit or adjustable to 90 if required? Also Monica: I'll share the DPA amendment draft for legal review. Anita: if you can confirm whether GreenBank is ok with 120-day snapshot purge or prefer a contractual requirement for 90 days, we can update the draft.

Thanks — attaching the retention table and DPA draft now.

Cheers,
Kimberly
Director, Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_retention_table.xlsx, dpa_amendment_draft.docx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carve-outs for marketplace backup windows

Kimberly / team — technical notes:

- Snapshot architecture: we use incremental EBS-style snapshots plus periodic full checkpoints stored in S3/GCS depending on region. Snapshots are immutable once created.
- Purge mechanics: object lifecycle rules in S3/GCS delete snapshot objects after X days; we also have a nightly reconciliation job that marks those deletions in our metadata service so audit events can be produced. In practice the snapshot purge window is 120 days by default (set in lifecycle policies).
- Guarantees & SLAs: we can move the lifecycle to 90 days, but there is a short blackout during which a snapshot required for a restore may not be immediately deletable (rare) — we can add process controls to avoid that for regulated customers.
- Deletion propagation: when a deletion request comes in we mark the customer id in a deletion index; the reconciliation job scans snapshots and flags objects for TTL deletion. We can provide a per-object deletion timestamp and a signed event log for compliance.
- Debug traces: recommend creating a separate per-customer bucket with its own lifecycle (TTL = 45 days). Access control via IAM roles; we can enforce that only redwood-sre+redwood-legal can access for the first 30 days and require explicit DPO approval afterwards.
- Cross-region transfers: snapshots may be copied across regions for DR; we can restrict copies to US/EU regions for GreenBank and include that in the DPA.

I'll prepare the short tech appendix for the DPA describing lifecycle rules and the event audit format.

—Marcus
VP, Platform Engineering
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-04T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carve-outs for marketplace backup windows

Thanks team — legal position and recommended edits: 

- DPA amendment: include explicit language: (a) primary data deletion within 90 days of request; (b) snapshot/backups purged within 120 days by default but can be reduced to 90 for regulated customers by written amendment; (c) debug-trace bucket TTL configurable with customer opt-in, default 45 days.
- Subprocessors: include a current list and commit to notify GreenBank 30 days prior to adding a subprocessor that will process customer data.
- Auditability: Redwood must provide an audit CSV for deletion events (object id, snapshot id, deletion timestamp, operator id) within 5 business days of request.

I'll attach a DPA amendment draft (dpa_amendment_draft.docx) with the above language. Marcus: please include the tech appendix describing the reconciliation job and the audit CSV schema. Kimberly: let's suggest GreenBank a trial of the 45-day debug TTL with weekly purge reports for the first 3 months.

Monica
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: dpa_amendment_draft.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@greenbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-05T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carve-outs for marketplace backup windows

Hi Anita — following up with Redwood's proposed contractual position and next steps. TL;DR included below and attachments included (subprocessor list).

Proposed contract language summary: 
- Active data: customer-initiated deletions complete within 90 days (applies to live stores and metadata).
- Backups/snapshots: default purge at 120 days, but Redwood will agree to a written amendment to reduce to 90 days for GreenBank specifically.
- Debug traces: per-customer debug-trace bucket with TTL of 45 days available as an opt-in security feature; access restricted and auditable.
- Subprocessors: attached redwood_subprocessors_v4.pdf (current list). Redwood will commit to 30 days' notice for material changes.
- Auditability: Redwood will provide an audit CSV for deletion events on request within 5 business days.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm whether GreenBank is satisfied with 90-day contractual commit for backups, or if you need further concessions.
2) If acceptable, sign the DPA amendment via DocuSign (link below) and we'll schedule a short tech review with Marcus for the audit CSV / purge report formats.

DocuSign (DPA amendment): https://docusign.net/REDW-4492
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/DBL-789

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_v4.pdf, proposed_retention_table.xlsx, dpa_amendment_draft.docx

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if that helps.

Best,
Kimberly
Director, Enterprise Accounts
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@greenbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: GreenBank IT <itops@greenbank.com>, External DPO <dpo@thirdparty.com>
Date: 2025-04-07T17:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention carve-outs for marketplace backup windows

Kimberly — apologies for the delay, legal had a couple of micro-asks but we can proceed: 

- GreenBank accepts the 90-day contractual commitment for backups for this engagement (please reflect in the DPA amendment).
- We accept the 45-day debug-trace TTL as an opt-in, provided debug traces are stored in a per-customer isolated bucket and access requires DPO sign-off after 30 days.
- Please ensure all subprocessors listed will process data only in US/EU for GreenBank; if any subprocessor does cross-region copies, we need explicit confirmation and prior notice.
- As an operational control, GreenBank requests weekly purge reports for the first 3 months after go-live (CSV listing deletion events). After that, monthly reports for 9 months.

We will route the DPA to our procurement team for signature via the DocuSign link. Our deal id for internal tracking: GB-2025-0412. 

Thanks — Anita
Security PM, GreenBank
